title: A bill to enhance whistleblower protection for contractor and grantee employees.
official_summary:
(This measure has not been amended since it was reported to the Senate on June 7, 2016. The summary of that version is repeated here.)

(Sec. 1) This bill extends federal contractor whistle-blower protections to employees of: (1) personal services contractors working on defense contracts (currently, the protections apply to employees of defense contractors, subcontractors, grantees, or subgrantees); and (2) personal services contractors or subgrantees working on federal civilian contracts (currently, the protections apply to employees of civilian contractors, subcontractors, or grantees). The civilian contractor protections, which are currently in effect as a pilot program, are made permanent.

The bill extends the prohibition against reimbursement of legal fees incurred in defending against reprisal claims brought by whistle-blowers to defense and civilian subcontractors and personal services contractors.

summary.headline: This law expands whistleblower protections for employees of certain federal contractors and grantees, and makes a civilian pilot program permanent.
summary.what_it_does: The law extends existing whistleblower protections to employees of personal services contractors working on defense contracts and on federal civilian contracts. It also extends those protections to subgrantees on civilian contracts. A pilot program that protected civilian contractor employees is made permanent. The law also extends a rule barring reimbursement of legal fees that companies spend defending against whistleblower reprisal claims to defense and civilian subcontractors and personal services contractors.

who_it_affects.group: Employees of personal services contractors working on defense contracts
who_it_affects.how: They gain the same whistleblower protections that employees of defense contractors, subcontractors, grantees, and subgrantees already had.

who_it_affects.group: Employees of personal services contractors and subgrantees working on federal civilian contracts
who_it_affects.how: They gain whistleblower protections that previously applied to employees of civilian contractors, subcontractors, and grantees.
Their whistleblower protections were a temporary pilot program, and the law makes those protections permanent.

who_it_affects.group: Defense and civilian subcontractors and personal services contractors
who_it_affects.how: They are barred from being reimbursed by the government for legal fees spent defending against whistleblower reprisal claims, the same limit that already applied to other contractors.
